sentence: This project studies how receiving breast cancer care across multiple health systems affects cancer outcomes for patients.
This project studies how a protein network controls the choices blood stem cells make, which may protect against clonal hematopoiesis.
This project studies how the sensory neurons in the mosquito biting apparatus detect blood and shape blood-feeding behavior.
This project studies how key regulators of gene expression are themselves regulated as stem cells make fate decisions.
This project provides core services to evaluate cellular abnormalities in diseases of stem cells and aging.
This project designs and tests trimers meant to guide memory B cells toward becoming fully mature producers of bNAb responses.
This project tries to find a functional cure for HIV by targeting an inhibitory pathway with an antibody combined with therapy and vaccination.
This project develops therapies to decrease venous neointimal hyperplasia and venous stenosis after angioplasty of hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulae.
This project develops lightsheet imaging methods that improve speed and resolution and can tell apart many cell types in cleared tissue.
This project studies a molecular pathway that controls how fat cells store and release fat, and whether it matters during fasting, obesity and aging.
This project studies how DNA oxidation and repair change chromatin to control gene expression in lung cells during hypoxia.
This project tests whether retinal biomarkers agree with brain imaging biomarkers for finding Alzheimer's disease risk before symptoms appear.
This project builds a tool that estimates a patient's chance of carrying a germline cancer susceptibility variant, using tumor sequencing data and family history.
This project uses machine learning to study what makes some words harder to learn to read than others.
This project carries out clinical trials on preventing, treating and curing HIV infection.
This project provides data management and statistical support for Alzheimer's disease research and builds methods to evaluate cognitive decline.
This project develops and applies computational methods to study complex diseases like cancer, heart disease and diabetes using large sequencing and imaging data sets.
This project studies how nerves and cancer influence each other through interoception, using genetically engineered mouse models of lung, pancreatic and colon cancers.
This project builds a computational platform that combines imaging, omics and genetic data to find early tissue vulnerability and discover drug repurposing options.
This project develops a dual-contrast agent imaging method to detect pyruvate metabolism and urea tissue-perfusion in prostate cancer patients to guide biopsies.
